steps.caption: One SQL primary handles every read and write. 3k rps at 90% reads: ρ 0.6.
9k rps. The primary can do 5k: it saturates.
Add 2 read replicas. Reads spread over 3 nodes; writes still go to the primary. The primary now sees 0.9k writes + 2.7k reads.
Writes rise to 50% (4.5k/s). Replicas can't take writes, so the primary saturates, and replicas fall behind: watch repl. lag grow.
Drop to 4k rps. Lag shrinks only once the primary has headroom. Until then, a user can write and then read stale data from a replica.
